title: Bounded Response Architecting — personal ideation pad
content:
Goal and why: sketch a lightweight feature that lets product teams specify hard/soft "bounded responses" per route or persona so we can meet latency SLOs and predictable token spend without breaking UX. This is me thinking aloud — rough PRD + user stories + experiments.

Problem statement:
- We have unpredictable tail latency and token spend for some flows (search summaries, customer support recaps, webhook-driven automation).
- Customers want guarantees: e.g., 95th percentile < 300ms or token spend under a budget per session.
- Current knobs (temperature, max_tokens) are blunt and break quality. Need a richer control surface that is fast to adopt.

Core idea: Bounded responses = declarative policy object attached to a route/model that expresses: max_tokens_budget (hard), latency_target_ms (soft), graceful_degradation_priority (list: shorten, compress, use cached prefix, fallback-model), fidelity_profile (high/medium/low), glance-summary-length (characters). The runtime enforces these at inference time: apply compression heuristics, switch to short-form decoding, or route to cheaper variant.

User stories:
- As a product manager, I want to attach a bounded response policy to the /assistant/quick-summary route so that we never exceed $X per session.
- As an engineer, I want the SDK to expose an API to fetch the current effective budget and decisions to surface in logs for debugging.
- As an SRE, I want a diagnostic mode that simulates policy decisions for the last 24h traffic without affecting live responses.

Acceptance criteria (MVP):
- Policy schema v0 (JSON) + UI minimal editor in Console (form).
- Runtime will enforce max_tokens_budget per request (hard stop) and attempt one of degradation strategies if budget exceeded.
- Telemetry: per-request policy id, reason code for each degradation action, token savings estimate.
- E2E test harness that runs a 10k-sample synthetic trace and validates that 99% of requests respect the budget.

Degradation strategies (ordered):
1) Use prefix truncation guided by semantic salience (cheap NLU score).
2) Switch to short-format template (pre-baked compressed prompts).
3) Route to an abridged model variant (e.g., quantized small).
4) Fall back to cached summary if available.

UX notes:
- Console should show estimated quality delta (heuristic) for each strategy so PMs can choose tradeoffs.
- SDK: response object contains policy_applied boolean and a human-readable justification string.
- For interactive flows, provide a small micro-recap with an affordance to "expand" (which can bill extra tokens).

Metrics to track:
- %requests that hit budget and were degraded.
- Quality regression delta vs baseline (BLEU/ROUGE or custom eval set).
- Token savings and cost delta.
- Latency percentiles before/after.

Experiment matrix (first 2 weeks after MVP):
- A/B test: bounded_response ON vs OFF on 2k weekly active sessions for a support-recap route. Measure quality, cost, retention.
- Degradation strategy order variants: truncation-first vs model-fallback-first.

Risks and open questions:
- Quality estimation: how to predict perceptual loss when compressing? Need a small eval harness and human-in-the-loop checks.
- Complexity of policy combinatorics for routes + persona + customer overrides. Maybe only allow one policy per route for MVP.
- Billing implications for "expand" affordance — need legal/finance input.
- Edge cases where shortening breaks downstream tools (parsers). Add a compatibility flag (structured-output-safe).

Implementation sketch (tech notes):
- Policy stored in control-plane (db row) with immutable version id.
- Router attaches policy id to request metadata. Runtime checks budget before decode and triggers strategy.
- Telemetry: emit policy_decision event to datastream (kafka) with tags: policy_id, decision, tokens_before, tokens_after, reason_code.
- Local dev: provide an SDK fixture that simulates each degradation strategy to help UX teams review.

Next steps / TODOs:
- Quick sync with Maya + Arjun to align telemetry fields (blocked: event schema). (TODO: schedule 30m)
- Draft policy JSON schema and add to /specs/policy-bounded-response.md (first pass).
- Wire a small Console prototype: form + estimate preview using a small eval prompt.
- Create a Linear board (or GitHub issue list) for the experiment tasks: infra, runtime, ui, eval, legal.

Notes to self:
- Keep initial surface small: single route attach, only hard max_tokens + 3 degradation strategies.
- Avoid fancy autoscaling coupling in MVP — the feature should work with existing routing.
- Put an obvious opt-out header for customers who don't want auto-degradation.

Random thoughts:
- Could allow user-visible "confidence bar" so clients can decide whether to request expansion.
- Maybe tie to Dedicated customers as a premium: guaranteed budget with higher fidelity.

Links / references I want to read before rough spec:
- Quick notes from infra on token accounting (link shared in Slack)
- Prior thread: #inference-budgeting-ideas (search for 2024-11-19)

End of pad. This is seeded for a draft PRD and will be cleaned up after the sync.
